watches.name: UTILITY 40 | CORE COLLECTION | TiX TITANIUM BRACELET
watches.description: For the full experience, upgrade your watch by adding our custom-fitted bracelet. Made from TiX hardened titanium, it’s solid and reliable, but light enough to disappear on your wrist. Titanium is hypoallergenic and shrugs off corrosion, so it’s perfect for handling sweat, saltwater and long days out. It’s built properly. Quick-release end links let you switch to a strap in seconds. Screw links and the included screwdriver let you size it easily in minutes. There's a half link for a dialled-in fit. And if the day warms up and your wrist follows suit, a hidden comfort link under the clasp gives you a 5mm on-the-fly extension. It completes the watch, takes the punishment, and outlasts anything you can throw at it. Note: This model is compatible with CORE collection watches in Granite, Forest, Ember and Cobalt colour-ways. (Serial numbers starting OC)

watches.name: Ontic Utility - 40mm Men's Titanium Watch - Black/Orange - Swiss Solar - 300m Water Resistant - British Built
watches.description: KEY FEATURES 40mm TiX Titanium case, hardened to 1200hv 300m water resistance FKM rubber strap, with option to add additional TiX Titanium bracelet Swiss solar-quartz movement For those who go out when others stay in Mountain Rescue teams go out in the worst conditions the UK can throw at them. Quietly, without fuss, and without any expectation of thanks. This watch is a nod to that spirit. Ontic’s founder, John, is a former Mountain Rescue volunteer. He learned the hard way that when the rain is sideways and the light is fading, your kit cannot be decorative. It has to work. So the MR1 is built the same way. TiX titanium (hardened to 1200HV). Swiss Solar movement. High contrast dial. 300 metre water resistance. Everything on it earns its place, including the bright orange and yellow accents which are inspired by the livery of UK Mountain Rescue vehicles. £40 from each watch supports Mountain Rescue England and Wales and Scottish Mountain Rescue. It's a small contribution to the teams who step into bad weather on purpose and bring people home.
